newsitem.title: USA: RTRS-Foster's has flat Molson outlook.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Foster's has flat Molson outlook.

text.p: Australian-based Foster's Brewing Group Ltd said it expected profitability of it 40 per cent-owned Molson Breweries to remain "constrained".

Foster's chief executive Ted Kunkel said on Wednesday that "we stubbed our toe" on Molson during the past year but said a major restructuring of the Canadian-based company would restore its underlying profitability.
Molson Breweries is also 40 percent-owned by Molson Cos Ltd , with the remainder held by Philip Morris Co.
"At Molson the past year has been a difficult one," Kunkel told a luncheon at the McIntosh Securities Investment Conference in New York.
"We lost some market share in Quebec in a shrinking market."
He said he was confident the appointment of a new management team, a decentralisation of the organisation's structure and a new emphasis on Molson's core brands would help turn its fortunes around.
"Looking ahead, though, the profitability of Molson will continue to be constrained by the competitive nature of the Canadian market," Kunkel said.
"Even so, Molson will remain a high return business.
"Foster's expects to receive no less than the return which has been generated over the past four years - that is approximately 20 per cent of the capital employed."
The Canadian brewer said on August 8 that first quarter revenue was relatively flat at C$589.6 million, compared to $590.1 million in the first quarter of last year.
Net profit fell to C$59.4 million in the latest three months ended July 1 from C$60.4 million a year earlier.
The company said it faced a 5.2 percent decline in volume in the latest period and its market share eased to 46.1 percent from 46.7 percent, including imports.
